s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic ankle pain and swelling with bony lesion
salient_findings: Pain and swelling around the right ankle for 1 year
Bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
Submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin
key_facts: 1-year history of pain and swelling around the right ankle
Bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
Ankle and subtalar joints have a full range of motion
Complete blood count within normal limits
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 68 mm at the first hour
Submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin

shortlist.label: Brodie's abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the diagnosis made based on clinical and radiographic findings

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with chronic infection and bone involvement

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible consideration given the age and location of the lesion

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, remains a consideration for a bone lesion in a young patient

shortlist.label: Chondroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the location and characteristics of the lesion

raw.rationale: The presence of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion with a well-defined sclerotic margin and an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate is consistent with a chronic bone infection, which is characteristic of Brodie's abscess.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: While osteomyelitis could explain some symptoms, the specific radiographic findings and the lack of systemic infection signs make Brodie's abscess a more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: Ewing's sarcoma typically presents with more aggressive features and systemic symptoms, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: Osteosarcoma usually presents with a more destructive and aggressive radiographic appearance, which does not match the well-defined sclerotic margin seen in this case.

rejected.label: Chondroblastoma
rejected.why: Chondroblastoma is a rare tumor that typically occurs in the epiphyses of long bones and has distinct radiographic and histological features not described in this vignette.
